finding_dispositions.evidence: Initialization and object-publication paths mutate filesystem targets before rejecting symlinks or unsupported filesystems.
A fence observed expired at clock 200 becomes valid again after rollback to 120 because the read path does not persist the high-water.
Separate resource-lock acquisitions accept resource-b followed by resource-a.
A caller-built claim omitting an action resource commits successfully and does not freeze that resource after lease expiry.
The doctor read-only role successfully executes WITH ... UPDATE and persists repository changes.
recover() returns a forged transaction head without validating it against the authoritative event stream and task head.

findings.summary: Filesystem validation is not mutation-before-use safe and can modify paths outside the repository through symlinks.
findings.evidence: In storage/graph_engineering/storage/connection.py:486-504, initialize() calls mkdir/chmod before lstat verification and probes the database before factory layout verification. An owner-only repository with objects -> external-dir changed the external target from 0755 to 0700 before RepositoryConfigurationError; repository.sqlite3 -> external-file changed the external file from 0644 to 0600. An unsupported-filesystem probe rejected only after creating root, locks, objects, staging, and repository.sqlite3. storage/graph_engineering/storage/objects.py:51-66 has the same fanout pattern: a fanout symlink changed an external directory to 0700 and left one staging file before rejection. Fresh verifier and all 150 tests still passed.
findings.required_fix: Validate every existing component with descriptor-relative, no-follow operations before chmod/open/write; use fstat/fchmod only on verified descriptors, verify all ancestors, and probe filesystem capability before repository mutation. Ensure unsupported filesystems and symlinked database/directory/fanout inputs cause zero external or repository side effects. Add regressions asserting external modes/bytes and repository contents remain unchanged.

findings.summary: Repository clock rollback can revive a lease that was already observed expired.
findings.evidence: storage/graph_engineering/storage/clock.py persists clock_high_water_ns only when advance=True, while ResourceLeaseRepository.validate_fence calls trusted_now(..., advance=False). Counterexample: lease issued at 100 with expires_at 150; validation at 200 returned false, then after wall-clock rollback to 120 the same lease/fence returned true. This violates the persisted non-decreasing high-water and no-revival requirements in Spec §5.4 and Test Plan §9.5.
findings.required_fix: Make every authoritative expiry decision use and atomically persist a non-decreasing repository high-water, including validation paths, or provide an equivalent durable monotonic mechanism. Add exact false-at-later-time then rollback regression proving the same lease can never become valid again.

findings.summary: Global canonical ordering is not enforced across separate resource-lock acquisitions.
findings.evidence: storage/graph_engineering/storage/locks.py checks only numeric lock ranks across held tokens. acquire_resources(('resource-b',)) followed by acquire_resources(('resource-a',)) was accepted because both have rank 1. This violates ADR-0002's canonical resource-ID ascending order and permits opposing callers to hold resources in inverse order, causing avoidable contention or retry exhaustion.
findings.required_fix: Either require all resource locks to be acquired through one atomic acquire-many call, or compare canonical resource IDs across the complete held/new token sequence and reject non-increasing acquisition before touching process or OS locks. Add same-thread and two-process b-then-a versus a-then-b regressions.

findings.summary: A public CommitBatch can forge an incomplete durable action claim and release an action resource after lease expiry.
findings.evidence: TaskRepository._insert_claim validates only the resources supplied in claim_delta; it does not compare them with the complete lease_resources set. I acquired a lease for resource-a and task:task-1, committed an action.execution_started event with a caller-built claim containing only task:task-1, advanced to expiry, and successfully granted resource-a to task-2 while claim-1 remained unresolved. CommitBatch and claim_delta are ordinary public data, so ResourceLeaseRepository.claim_action is not an enforceable boundary.
findings.required_fix: Inside the atomic commit, derive or require exact equality between claim resources/fences and the complete attested lease resource/fence set, bind the claim lease to the task lease assertion, and reject omitted, extra, empty, stale, or mismatched sets. Add direct CommitBatch counterexamples rather than testing only the helper-generated claim.

findings.summary: Doctor and backup roles are not actually read-only because the SQL prefix gate accepts data-changing WITH statements.
findings.evidence: ManagedConnection._check_statement allows WITH for doctor/backup based only on the first token. Using factory.open('doctor'), `WITH probe AS (SELECT 1) UPDATE schema_versions SET version='forged' WHERE component='storage'` executed and persisted successfully. This violates the minimum-role and read-only connection contract despite the existing direct DELETE negative test.
findings.required_fix: Open read-only roles with an enforceable SQLite read-only/query_only boundary and an authorizer or semantic statement check that rejects all write opcodes, including WITH-prefixed UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT and side-effecting constructs. Add doctor and backup regressions for each disguised write form.

findings.summary: Transaction recovery trusts redundant transaction metadata without authoritative replay validation.
findings.evidence: TaskRepository.recover reads revision/head_digest directly from transactions. After a valid commit, changing that row's head_digest to sha256-jcs-v1 followed by 64 zeroes caused recover('tx') to return the forged COMMITTED head, although replay correctly detects the inconsistency. This contradicts corruption fail-closed and exact event/transaction/head binding requirements.
findings.required_fix: Before returning COMMITTED, validate the transaction record against its exact event batch, revision, transaction head, task history and authoritative committed head/replay state; malformed or inconsistent records must raise integrity-blocked rather than return success. Bind this with transaction revision, head, task and event-index corruption regressions against recover(), not only replay().
